guide.summary: Customers should authorize a public Notion integration through the OAuth flow, with each user selecting shared pages in the page picker. The integration needs only the Read content capability; Insert and Update content should stay off. Because customers in other workspaces will connect, the integration must be public, not limited to selected workspaces. Read content is documented for the page markdown endpoint. Title retrieval is documented through the page endpoint, but its capability mapping is not stated in the supplied passages, so it stays unresolved. Enumerating every page a customer shared is not documented in the supplied sources.

steps.title: Implement the callback and code-to-token exchange
steps.detail: Implement the redirect handler that receives the code and exchanges it at the token endpoint with Basic client credentials. Do not run the exchange until a customer has consented.

This endpoint is described in more detail in the API reference docs for creating a token .

steps.title: Authorize a test workspace user and select a test page
steps.detail: Using a representative test workspace user, open the authorization URL, select a test page the user has full access to, approve, and run the code exchange. Authorization alone is not a resource test.
steps.doneWhen: An access token is returned for the test user and the selected page is shared with the integration.

steps.doneWhen: The response includes a markdown field containing the page content.

page_id: "b55c9c91-384d-452b-81db-d1ef79372b75" }) console . log ( response . markdown )
Set the markdown_version query parameter to v2 to get Notion-flavored Markdown instead. v2 is recommended. v1 is deprecated. It’s the default on current Notion-Versions. See Markdown versions .

steps.title: Read the title of a customer-shared page
steps.detail: Retrieve one page the customer explicitly shared with the connection, using the page ID as input and filter_properties=title so only the title property is returned. Representative input: a shared page ID from the customer's selection. Expected result: a 200 response whose properties object contains the title. Use only GET. Boundary check: use a real page in the same workspace that the customer did not share, then confirm the response is 404 and no page content is returned. Confirm the request log contains only this GET request and no write.
steps.doneWhen: The response for the shared page includes the page title in the title property. The unshared page check returns 404 with no content, and the request log shows only GET requests.

evidence.quote: string required The ID of the page to retrieve.
Pages that aren't in a data source always return only title .
​ Errors The connection needs read content capabilities . Missing capabilities return 403 . A missing page or missing access returns 404 .
